title: Unit 1 Review
subject: Career Planning
directions: Answer each question to earn points. If you miss one, you will see a tip and can review the lesson.

items.prompt: Why is it useful to know your interests, strengths, and values when planning a career?

choices.text: They help you choose work that fits you
They guarantee you the highest-paying job
They replace the need to research careers
They only matter once you already work

items.explanation: Knowing yourself helps you aim for careers that match your interests, strengths, and values.

items.objective: Researching careers and the job market
items.prompt: Which actions help you research careers and the changing job market? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Look up the skills and education a career usually needs
Check whether demand for that work is rising or falling
Assume popular careers will never change over time
Compare pay, duties, and work settings across careers

items.explanation: Strong career research covers skills, education, demand, pay, and day-to-day work.

items.objective: Researching careers and the job market
items.prompt: What is one reason the job market can change over time?

choices.text: New technology can change which jobs exist
Every career stays exactly the same forever
Job research only helps after you retire
Pay stays the same in every career field

items.explanation: Technology, demand, and other shifts can change which careers grow or shrink.

items.prompt: Match each education or training path to what it usually means.

pairs.right: Learn a trade while working with a mentor
Short training for a specific skill or job
A college program that usually takes two years
A college program that usually takes four years

items.explanation: Different careers need different training paths, from certificates to degrees and apprenticeships.

items.prompt: What should you compare when choosing an education or training path?

choices.text: How well it fits the career, your goals, and cost
Which school campus has the nicest buildings
Whether your friends already finished that path
Which program title sounds the most impressive

items.explanation: A good training path fits the job requirements and is realistic for your time, goals, and budget.

items.prompt: Sort each item into the group where it belongs.

cards.text: Set a short-term step toward a career
Track monthly expenses while in school
Break a big goal into smaller milestones
Plan how to pay for tools or supplies

items.explanation: Career planning includes clear goals and a realistic look at costs and budgeting.

items.prompt: What makes a career goal more useful?

choices.text: It is clear and has steps you can take
It is vague and has no next step yet
It ignores time and money on purpose
It only counts if someone else picks it

items.explanation: Useful goals are clear and include steps you can actually take.

feedback.outOfTries: Here's a tip. Review the lesson, then continue.
